clinicalPearls: Hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia is characterised by the classic triad of hypohidrosis, hypotrichosis and hypodontia arising from defective development of ectodermal appendages.
The commonest form is X-linked, caused by variants in EDA (ectodysplasin A); autosomal dominant and recessive forms result from EDAR, EDARADD and WNT10A variants.
Reduced or absent eccrine sweat glands cause heat intolerance and recurrent unexplained hyperthermia, which can be life-threatening in infancy.
Characteristic facies include frontal bossing, a depressed nasal bridge, periorbital hyperpigmentation and full everted lips.
Teeth are absent or few and conical or peg-shaped, prompting early prosthodontic planning and later consideration of implants.
Deficient mucous and seromucous glands cause dry eyes, dry nasal and respiratory mucosa, atrophic rhinitis with crusting, and recurrent respiratory infection.
Female carriers of X-linked disease may show patchy or mosaic features owing to lyonisation.
WNT10A-related disease can present with a milder or oligodontia-predominant phenotype that overlaps with tooth-agenesis syndromes.
reference.pathophysiology: Hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia is a disorder of the ectodysplasin signalling pathway, which governs the reciprocal epithelial-mesenchymal interactions that pattern and elaborate ectodermal appendages including hair follicles, teeth, and eccrine, sebaceous, salivary, lacrimal and mucous glands. Ectodysplasin A, a tumour necrosis factor family ligand encoded by EDA on the X chromosome, binds its receptor EDAR, which signals through the adaptor EDARADD to activate NF-kappa-B and thereby drive appendage placode formation and differentiation; the WNT pathway, including WNT10A, feeds into and reinforces this programme. Loss-of-function variants at any point interrupt placode induction so that sweat glands are hypoplastic or absent, hair is sparse and fine, and teeth fail to develop normally, producing conical crowns and hypodontia or anodontia. Diminished eccrine function impairs evaporative cooling and causes dangerous hyperthermia, while hypoplasia of mucous and seromucous glands leaves the ocular, nasal, oral and respiratory surfaces dry and vulnerable to crusting and infection. X-linked inheritance predominates, with carrier females variably affected through random X-inactivation.
additionalDifferentials: Ectrodactyly-ectodermal dysplasia-clefting and other TP63-related ectodermal dysplasias
Incontinentia pigmenti in the context of NF-kappa-B pathway disease
Isolated non-syndromic hypodontia or oligodontia (including WNT10A-related tooth agenesis)
additionalInvestigations: Molecular genetic testing of EDA, EDAR, EDARADD and WNT10A tailored to the inheritance pattern
Assessment of sweating capacity, including sweat pore evaluation or pilocarpine-based testing
Dental and panoramic radiographic assessment to map tooth agenesis
Ophthalmological evaluation of tear film and ocular surface
Immunological evaluation where features suggest the NEMO-related immunodeficiency variant
Genetic counselling with carrier assessment of at-risk female relatives in X-linked disease
redFlags: Unexplained recurrent hyperthermia or heat collapse in an infant, which may be fatal
Recurrent or severe respiratory infection, especially with associated immunodeficiency features
Failure to thrive in infancy related to feeding difficulty and recurrent illness
Severe atrophic rhinitis with airway crusting and obstruction
reference.prognosis: With early recognition, avoidance of heat stress and multidisciplinary dental, dermatological and ophthalmological care, most affected individuals have a normal lifespan, though undiagnosed infants are at real risk from hyperthermia and, in the immunodeficiency-associated form, from severe infection.
pitfalls: Attributing recurrent infantile fevers to infection and missing the underlying hypohidrosis
Overlooking mildly or mosaically affected carrier females and thus miscounselling on inheritance
Assuming all cases are X-linked and neglecting autosomal WNT10A, EDAR and EDARADD forms
Failing to screen for the NEMO-associated immunodeficiency phenotype when infections are prominent
Delaying prosthodontic and dental planning that materially affects nutrition, speech and development
references: Dermatology and ectodermal dysplasia reference texts
management: Prevent and manage hyperthermia through heat avoidance, environmental cooling, hydration and wetting of skin and clothing, since absent sweat glands cause dangerous heat intolerance
Provide early prosthodontic care with dentures for the hypodontia, progressing to dental implants once growth allows
Treat dry eyes with ocular lubricants and manage the dry nasal and respiratory mucosa with saline irrigation, humidification and removal of crusts
Manage recurrent respiratory and skin infections promptly with appropriate antimicrobials
Educate carers and schools to recognise and treat overheating, particularly in infancy when hyperthermia can be life-threatening
Refer for multidisciplinary dermatology, dental, ophthalmology and ENT care
Evaluate immune function and involve clinical immunology where features suggest the NEMO-related immunodeficiency variant
Offer genetic counselling and carrier testing of at-risk female relatives in X-linked disease
